articles.title: Thousands of pregnant women at risk in Yemeni city of Taiz, UN agency says
articles.description: By Olivia Le PoidevinGENEVA, Nov 3 (Reuters) - Fighting and access restrictions in and around the Yemeni city ofTaiz have left more than 13,000 pregnant women without essential healthcare and are leading to more miscarriages, the United Nations Population Fund said on Tuesday.Taiz has been largely isolated for a month, with fighting preventing humanitarian supplies from entering and civilians from leaving, following an escalation in clashes between the Saudi-backed government and the Iran-aligned Houthi movement.

articles.title: Higher oil prices boost Saudi Aramco profits despite disruption from attacks
articles.description: Saudi Aramco is reporting a 35% increase in third-quarter net profit, boosted by higher oil prices and the sale of a stake in a Malaysian company. Net profit rose to $36.3 billion from $26.9 billion a year earlier. Adjusted net profit, excluding the sale, increased 9% to $31.2 billion. The company benefitted from high profit margins at its refineries. Oil prices surged after the Iran war began in February, disrupting supply. Saudi Aramco maintained exports using its East-West pipeline despite attacks. The company remains a major revenue source for the Saudi government.

articles.title: Gulf Arab states struggle under the cloud of war
articles.description: Many places in the Persian Gulf like Dubai, Qatar, and Saudi Arabia, have spent decades modernizing and inviting investment from around the world. But that effort has been stymied by wars that have landed on their doorstep– including conflicts in Yemen and Iran.We go to Saudi Arabia’s capital, Riyadh, to hear how these wars are threatening the kingdom’s plans for the future.  And we hear how other Gulf states are worried about the possibility of renewed attacks on Iran and the retaliation that could follow.Support public media with NPR+ and enjoy perks for over 25 podcasts like this one.
